headline: RIO TINTO OPENS TWO NEW ARGENTINA LITHIUM PLANTS WORTH $1.4B — Fénix 1B, Sal de Vida Add 25,000 t LCE/Year; Milei Joins Ceremony
snippet: Rio Tinto officially opened its Fénix 1B expansion (10,000 t LCE/yr) and Sal de Vida (15,000 t LCE/yr) projects in Catamarca province on October 28–29, joined by Argentine President Javier Milei and CEO Simon Trott. The $1.4 billion combined investment marks the largest foreign mining commitment to Argentina since President Milei's RIGI incentive regime took effect; Rio Tinto is now weighing a further $1 billion Fénix II phase targeting a RIGI filing in 2027, part of a $4.4 billion Argentina pipeline aimed at 200,000 t LCE/year by 2028.

headline: AUSTRALIA BACKS DONALD RARE EARTHS WITH A$180M GOVERNMENT DEBT — Energy Fuels/Astron Project to Be World's 4th-Largest Outside China
snippet: Energy Fuels and Astron Corporation received conditional credit approval for up to A$180 million (US$126M) from two Australian government financing institutions for the Donald Project in western Victoria — the country's first commercial rare earths mine. Phase 1 targets 9,000 tonnes per year of rare earth element concentrate with a 40-year mine life; once built, Donald will rank as the world's fourth-largest rare earths operation outside China. Production is planned as early as 2027, and the rare earth concentrate will be shipped to Energy Fuels' White Mesa mill in Utah for separation.

headline: FED HOLDS RATES 3.75–4.00%, TWO HAWKISH DISSENTS SIGNAL DECEMBER HIKE — Gold Steadies, Silver Extends Losses
snippet: The Federal Reserve voted to hold the fed funds rate at 3.75–4.00% at its October 28 FOMC meeting, but two committee members dissented in favour of an immediate 25-basis-point hike — the second straight meeting with hawkish dissent under Chair Kevin Warsh. Markets are now pricing an over 80% probability of a December hike following the vote and the next morning's 3.4% Q3 GDP print. Spot gold steadied near $4,050 on the decision before slipping further on the GDP news, while silver extended its fall toward $52 — a two-year low.

headline: COLLECTIVE MINING DRILLS 14.25m AT 6.49 g/t AuEq AT APOLLO SHALLOW HALO — High-Grade Colombia System Expands Near Surface (TSX:CNL)
snippet: Collective Mining (TSX: CNL) reported a new high-grade intersection of 14.25 metres at 6.49 g/t gold-equivalent at its Apollo Shallow Halo Zone in Colombia, expanding near-surface mineralisation within its flagship Aris-area project. The Apollo system — which has now produced multiple headline-grade intercepts at shallow depths — is one of the highest-priority drill targets in the junior sector for potential open-pit economics. Results were highlighted in Mining Stock Daily's October 27 morning briefing.

headline: GOLD MINERS TRADE AT HISTORIC DISCOUNT — NEWMONT, AGNICO AT 9–15x FORWARD EARNINGS VS. COPPER NAMES AT 21–24x
snippet: An Investing.com analysis finds gold producers are among the most deeply discounted equities in the mining sector: Newmont, Kinross and Agnico Eagle trade at 9–15x forward earnings after a 25–30% selloff from January highs, while copper names Freeport-McMoRan and Southern Copper fetch 21–24x. The piece calls out Newmont specifically as a standout value given its scale and cost guidance, noting RSI readings of 28–33 across the group — extreme oversold territory — though it cautions these readings alone are not reversal signals at current rate-hike odds.

headline: TREY REIK: GOLD BROKE $4,000 — 'THE FED JUST PROVED ME RIGHT' ON STRUCTURAL BULL CASE
snippet: Precious metals strategist Trey Reik argues the October FOMC decision — a hold with two hawkish dissents — is a structural positive for gold long-term, even as the metal tests the $4,000 floor. His key data point: gold-backed ETF holdings continued rising through the 25% pullback from January highs, indicating institutional accumulation rather than capitulation. Reik notes the GDX miners index is down roughly 29% from highs versus gold's 25% — a tighter-than-usual gap he reads as a setup for leveraged equity outperformance on any metal recovery.

headline: LULA RE-ELECTED IN BRAZIL: WORLD'S #2 RARE EARTH RESERVE NATION DOUBLES DOWN ON DOMESTIC PROCESSING
snippet: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's re-election in Brazil's October 26 runoff positions the world's second-largest rare earth reserve nation as a potential counterweight to Chinese supply chain dominance — and a flashpoint with Washington. Lula has pledged to shield Brazil's rare earths from raw-export deals, favouring domestic processing partnerships; the US government already holds a 10% stake in USA Rare Earth's Serra Verde mine, which produces mixed heavy rare earth carbonate from ionic clay in Goiás. Canaccord Genuity analysts highlighted Power Minerals' Morro do Ferro project as an emergent rare earth watch post-election.

headline: FREEPORT Q3 EPS $0.88 BEATS ON COPPER AT $6.54/lb — 60K oz GOLD DEFERRED TO Q4, INDONESIA EXPORT DISPUTE LOOMS
snippet: Freeport-McMoRan's Q3 2026 adjusted EPS came in at $0.88 versus $0.50 a year earlier, driven by copper realised at $6.54 per pound (≈$14,400/t) on 749 million pounds sold. Gold sales fell sharply to 105,000 oz — roughly 60,000 oz were deferred into Q4 due to timing at PT Freeport Indonesia's newly restarted smelter — but copper revenue more than covered the gap. Full-year copper guidance stands at 3.0 billion pounds. A new Indonesia gold export dispute has emerged as a material risk for Q4.

headline: ELDORADO GOLD FIRST TWO SKOURIES FILTER PRESSES ONLINE — Four More Due November; European Copper-Gold Mine Nears Commercial Output (TSX:ELD)
snippet: Eldorado Gold (TSX: ELD) announced on October 26–27 that the first two of six Metso tailings filter presses at its Skouries copper-gold mine in northern Greece are now operational — a key commissioning milestone. Four operating presses are required for commercial sulphide production and five for nameplate throughput; Eldorado expects all remaining presses commissioned by November 2026. Skouries is one of Europe's largest undeveloped copper-gold systems and was permitted after more than a decade of permitting battles and delays.

headline: ELEMENTAL ROYALTY CLOSES $188M ORION ACQUISITION, CREDIT FACILITY UP TO $250M — Kouroussa Stream, Homestake Royalty Among Four Assets
snippet: Elemental Royalty (TSX: ELE) closed four of five royalty and streaming assets from Orion Mine Finance on October 26 for approximately US$188 million in cash plus 3.94 million shares, simultaneously upsizing its revolving credit facility to US$250 million. Assets acquired include the Kouroussa (Guinea) gold stream, the Ruby Hill / Granite Creek silver stream, the Homestake District (Nevada) royalty, and the La Negra royalty; a fifth asset — the Snowy River gold stream in New Zealand — is expected to close in Q1 2027. The total package, announced in September at US$290 million, transforms Elemental into a mid-tier royalty company with two near-producing cash-flow streams.
